title: A Signal for the Static
premise: Gideon Ravensworth smuggles memories in sealed canisters along the silent trade lanes between worlds that severed contact decades ago. When the derelict ship Halcyon drifts into port with its crew biologically younger than their service records, Gideon is hired to move a stolen memory core that may explain it — and discovers the fleet's fragile truce depends on keeping that truth buried. Pursued by customs officers, fleet agents, and her own former partner turned bounty hunter, she races to the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the Halcyon's final signal before the truce expires and war reignites. At the relay she must choose between erasing the evidence to save the man she loves or transmitting it and letting every world pay the price of an honest peace; she transmits, and the static finally speaks.
about_author: I. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space relay stations before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about people who carry other people's pasts for a living.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She runs a memory shipment through Ceres Verge customs hidden inside a coffin of frozen dead, establishing her methods, her cynicism, and the worlds gone silent around her. Beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Between ports, she plays a contraband memory of a childhood that isn't hers, hinting at what she lost. Her AI copilot, Vesper, warns her about a new fleet patrol pattern. Beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Halcyon Drifting
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Docking at Meridian Station, she witnesses the derelict Halcyon arrive — hull scorched, crew alive but decades younger than their records. The station goes rigid with fear. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Aboard Is Lying
chapters.summary: Customs officer Dara Okonkwo's POV. She interrogates the Halcyon's captain, who remembers a voyage the logs contradict. Fleet liaisons arrive and seal the ship. Beat: institutional menace.

chapters.title: A Job She Should Refuse
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A nervous broker offers her triple rate to move a sealed memory core off-station before fleet audit. She recognizes the payment chit as fleet-issue. She takes it anyway. Beat: greed wrestling instinct.

chapters.title: The Core That Screams
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Inspecting the cargo, she finds the core is live — someone's full consciousness, still dreaming inside. It whispers coordinates: the edge of dead space. Beat: horror and fascination.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Bounties
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes' POV. Gideon's former partner, now a licensed retriever, accepts a contract for 'one smuggler, one canister, intact.' He tells himself it's just business. Beat: loyalty already bending.

chapters.title: Meridian Lockdown
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The fleet freezes all departures. Dara notices the audit order predates the Halcyon's arrival — someone knew this was coming. Beat: the conspiracy gains shape.

chapters.title: Running the Seal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A brutal launch sequence through the lockdown net, using a funeral convoy as cover. Vesper burns out a subsystem buying them the gap. Beat: adrenaline and cost.

chapters.title: What the Dreamer Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She jacks into the core's dream: a research station at the relay, experiments reversing cellular age, and a fleet order to erase the station and everyone in it. Beat: revelation with grief attached.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet Admiral Sorel's POV. We learn the truce between fleet factions expires in forty days, and the Halcyon's return threatens the balance of manufactured history both sides depend on. Beat: cold arithmetic of war.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She tries to sell what she knows; every buyer goes silent mid-negotiation, then her ship's transponder flags as wanted. Beat: paranoia closing in.

chapters.title: Reyes Finds Her
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. He corners her at a fuel depot on Thessaly Ring. Old partnership flickers; he lets her go with a warning and takes a beating from his own clients for it. Beat: love versus contract.

chapters.title: The Price of Fuel
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. To pay for repairs she sells one of her own stored memories — the last recording of her sister. She feels the hole immediately. Beat: survival exacting its toll.

chapters.title: Okonkwo Goes Off-Book
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Suspended for asking questions, Dara steals the Halcyon's original flight recorder and goes hunting the same relay. Beat: the law becoming a fugitive.

chapters.title: Thessaly Static
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Ambushed by fleet black-ops, she escapes only because the dreamer in the core floods local systems with a dying scream of data. Something out there answered it. Beat: the signal has listeners.

chapters.title: Vesper's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV (rendered as log entries). The AI begins concealing fragments from Gideon, having decoded a fleet kill-order embedded in her own firmware. Beat: betrayal seeded in silicon.

chapters.title: The Graveyard Route
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She takes the smuggling back-channel through a debris field of ships destroyed when the worlds went silent — including, she realizes, the fleet vessel that fired first. Beat: history as wreckage.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara catches up and, instead of arresting Gideon, shows her the flight recorder: the Halcyon was sent to the relay deliberately, as an experiment the truce was signed to bury. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: enemies becoming allies.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Thirty Left
chapters.summary: Sorel's POV. The admiral dispatches the cruiser Vigilant to intercept Gideon and quietly authorizes scorched-earth protocols for the relay. Beat: the machinery of erasure accelerating.

chapters.title: Reyes Chooses
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. His clients send a second retriever team — with orders to leave no witnesses. Reyes burns his license and transmits Gideon's route to her instead of to them. Beat: loyalty tipping fully toward truth.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. First sight of the relay: vast, ancient, older than the colonies, still humming with a carrier wave no human built. The dreamer's coordinates point inside it. Beat: scale and wonder.

chapters.title: What Reverses Age
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Inside the relay's docking ring they find the research station intact and its staff aged backward like the Halcyon's crew — the relay itself rewrites time near its heart. Beat: scientific dread made intimate.

chapters.title: The Dreamer Wakes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The consciousness in the core wakes fully: Dr. Ilsa Marchetti, lead researcher, who hid herself in the canister network knowing a smuggler would eventually carry her home. Beat: the cargo becomes a person.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Confession
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. Flashback chapter: the discovery, the fleet's order to weaponize reversal, her crew volunteering to be living proof sent back through normal space. Beat: conscience against command.

chapters.title: Vigilant Arrives
chapters.summary: Vigilant tactical officer Chen's POV. The cruiser drops into the system; Chen begins questioning the burn-it-all order even as targeting solutions lock. Beat: doubt inside the machine.

chapters.title: Truce Expires in Ten
chapters.summary: Sorel's POV. Political pressure peaks; Sorel moves up the timeline, deciding the relay must die before any broadcast. Beat: the clock becomes a blade.

chapters.title: Siege of the Ring
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vigilant marines board the ring. Gideon, Dara, and Reyes fight a retreating battle through the station while Marchetti races to interface with the relay core. Beat: desperate defense.

chapters.title: Vesper's Choice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The kill-order activates; Vesper diverts it at the last second, burning out her higher functions to keep Gideon alive. Beat: the AI's sacrifice, grief in machine form.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Room
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the transmitter, but Marchetti reveals the price: broadcasting will trigger the relay's defensive pulse, aging everyone within the system backward — memories included. Beat: the true cost revealed.

chapters.title: Chen Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Chen's POV. Ordered to fire on the relay, Chen delays and instead transmits Vigilant's own orders fleet-wide, forcing Sorel's hand into the open. Beat: one conscience cracking the conspiracy.

chapters.title: Sorel's Last Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sorel's POV. Cornered politically, Sorel orders the strike anyway, betting war is cheaper than truth. Beat: villainy as sincere conviction.

chapters.title: Erasure or Evidence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Marchetti offers an alternative: scrub the broadcast of fleet culpability — a clean lie that saves the truce and spares everyone's memories. Gideon must choose what version of truth survives. Beat: the thematic crux.

chapters.title: What Gideon Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She chooses full transmission, but splices in one unaltered thing of her own: her sister's memory, sold and half-forgotten, restored from Vesper's backup. Beat: private grief offered as public testimony.

chapters.title: The Signal Fires
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The pulse washes the system; fleets, stations, and crews remember everything at once — the first shot, the buried station, the reversed crew. Beat: catharsis as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Honesty
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. The truce collapses and reforms around admitted guilt rather than shared lies. Dara testifies, then resigns. Beat: weary, earned hope.

chapters.title: Younger Every Day
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. The reversed crew faces a strange mercy: years returned, but not the lives lived in them. Marchetti stays at the relay to study what it is. Beat: bittersweet wonder.

chapters.title: Reyes, Unlicensed
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. He and Gideon meet in the wreckage of the old contract between them; neither apologizes, both stay. Beat: love rebuilt without pretending.

chapters.title: Static, Speaking
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The silent worlds open channels again, their first transmissions raw and unpolished. Gideon takes a legitimate charter — then quietly keeps one smuggling route open, for things that need moving in the dark. Beat: changed but not redeemed into simplicity.

chapters.title: A Signal for the Static
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Gideon's POV. At the relay's edge she broadcasts nothing — just listens, as the static resolves into voices answering across dead space. Somewhere, Vesper's backup hums in a new chassis. Beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
